1.note: The pronoun **I** refers to Qoheleth, the Teacher. Here, and other places throughout this chapter, it is stated separately from the verb for emphasis. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And I, the Teacher, turned]

Qoheleth says **all the oppressions** as an extreme statement for emphasis. He means very many oppressions, not necessarily every single one. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [very many oppressions]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **oppressions**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the oppressive acts]

The expression **were being done** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [people were doing]
See how you translated the phrase **under the sun** in 1:3 and use that here and elsewhere in this chapter.

Qoheleth is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [And consider this]

Here, **the tears of the oppressed** represents their grief and suffering. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the grief and suffering of the oppressed]

Here, **the hand** represents the power or control of the ones oppressing them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [From the power of those who oppressed them]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **strength**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [were cruel acts]

3.note: The expression **is being done** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [people are doing]

4.q: אֶת כָּל עָמָ֗ל וְ⁠אֵת֙ כָּל כִּשְׁר֣וֹן הַֽ⁠מַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה
4.note: The terms **every toil** and **every success of the deed** mean similar things. Solomon is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [all that they accomplished]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **success**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [successful result of]

Qoheleth is using the possessive form to describe a **deed** that is characterized by **envy of a person from his friend**, meaning that people’s work is driven by jealousy of their neighbors. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [is motivated by a person’s envy of his neighbor]
See how you translated this phrase in 1:14.

5.q: הַ⁠כְּסִיל֙ חֹבֵ֣ק אֶת יָדָ֔י⁠ו וְ⁠אֹכֵ֖ל אֶת בְּשָׂרֽ⁠וֹ
5.note: Qoheleth uses a proverb in order to illustrate the self-destructive nature of laziness. Translate this proverb in a way that will be recognized as a proverb and be meaningful in your language and culture. Alternate translation: [The fool folds his hands and eats his own flesh]

Qoheleth is using **is folding his hands** as a common expression of the culture to mean “is being lazy” or “is refusing to work.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [is being lazy]

Qoheleth is speaking as if the fool’s laziness were causing him to consume his own **flesh**. He means that the fool’s idleness destroys himself. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and is destroying himself]

6.q: ט֕וֹב מְלֹ֥א כַ֖ף נָ֑חַת מִ⁠מְּלֹ֥א חָפְנַ֛יִם עָמָ֖ל וּ⁠רְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ
6.note: Qoheleth uses a proverb in order to teach that contentment with little is better than striving for much. Translate this proverb in a way that will be recognized as a proverb and be meaningful in your language and culture. Alternate translation: [One handful with peace is better than two handfuls with toil and chasing after wind]

Qoheleth is speaking as if having a small amount with peace were having **a fullness of a palm with quiet**. He means that having few possessions and being content is valuable. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a small amount with peace]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **fullness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [than two hands filled]
See how you translated this phrase in 1:14.

7.note: See how you translated this in 1:14.

8.note: Qoheleth is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [he does not even have a son or a brother]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **toil**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the hard work he does]
Here, **his eye** represents his desire or appetite. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [he is never satisfied]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of wealth, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [with all that he owns]

8.q: וּ⁠לְ⁠מִ֣י אֲנִ֣י עָמֵ֗ל וּ⁠מְחַסֵּ֤ר אֶת נַפְשִׁ⁠י֙ מִ⁠טּוֹבָ֔ה
8.note: The lonely person is using the question form to emphasize that there is no good reason for his solitary toil. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [So there is no reason for me to toil and cause my soul to lack from good things.]
Here, **my soul** represents the person himself. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [myself]
See how you translated this in 1:14.
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of business, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and it is unpleasant to deal with]

9.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **wage**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to earn more]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **toil**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [in exchange for the work they do]

10.note: Qoheleth is presenting a possible condition, that if two companions fall, one can help the other up. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. Alternate translation: [For if one of them falls]

Qoheleth is using a phrase that expresses a strong feeling of distress for the person who is alone and falls with no one to help. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [but how terrible it will be for him]

12.note: The pronoun **he** refers to an attacker, while the pronoun **him** refers to the person who is alone. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And if an attacker overpowers the one person]

Qoheleth is speaking as if the bond between three people were a **three-fold rope** that cannot easily be **torn in two**. He means that three people united together are very strong. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and three people standing together will not be quickly defeated]

The expression **will not be torn in two** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [will not break in two]

13.q: ט֛וֹב יֶ֥לֶד מִסְכֵּ֖ן וְ⁠חָכָ֑ם מִ⁠מֶּ֤לֶךְ זָקֵן֙ וּ⁠כְסִ֔יל
13.note: Qoheleth uses a proverb in order to teach that wisdom is more valuable than power or age. Translate this proverb in a way that will be recognized as a proverb and be meaningful in your language and culture.

The expression **to be warned** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [to receive warnings]

14.note: Qoheleth is using **the house of those who are bound** as a common expression of the culture to mean “prison.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from prison]

The expression **who are bound** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [those whom someone had bound]
The pronoun **he** refers to the poor but wise youth from the previous verse. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the poor but wise youth came forth]

The expression **he was born** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [his mother bore him into poverty]

15.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 4:2.

The pronoun **him** refers to the young king mentioned in the previous verses. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [who will stand in his place as the next king]

16.note: Qoheleth says **There was no end to all the people** as an extreme statement for emphasis. He means that there were very many people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [There were very many people]
The pronoun **him** refers to the young king who rose to power. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [will not rejoice in that young king]
See how you translated the similar phrase in 1:14.
